name: United Rentals
description: United Rentals is the largest US equipment rental company, renting construction, industrial and specialty equipment from 1,768 locations to contractors, industrial firms and cities. It owns about $22.5B (at original cost) of fleet, 1.1 million units, and earns its money the way a landlord does: rental revenue is 86% of the total, fleet is bought with debt, rented at hourly/daily/weekly rates, and sold after a few years (used equipment sales were $1.4B in 2025). Profit depends on rental rates and how often each machine is on rent (time utilization), against a huge depreciation bill; adjusted EBITDA margin was 45.5% but that is before that depreciation, so operating margin is 24.7% ($3,973M of $16,099M). It estimates a 15% North American market share, so most of the market is still small local renters. Large customers matter: 69% of rental revenue is from key accounts, 46% from national accounts, yet the biggest single customer is 1% of revenue.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label from general knowledge; not re-checked against MSCI/S&P. SEC SIC 7359 (Equipment Rental & Leasing, NEC).

businessLines.name: General rentals
businessLines.how: Rental revenue per day/week/month on owned fleet, plus sales of used equipment, new equipment and contractor supplies; profit is rental rate times utilization minus depreciation and delivery costs.
businessLines.description: General construction and industrial equipment (aerial work platforms, forklifts, earthmoving, compaction, power, etc.) rented across the US, Canada and Europe.

operatingProfit.note: United Rentals reports segment equipment rentals gross profit (not segment operating income); this is the profit measure shown, before selling, general and administrative and other costs. Share is of the $5,248M total equipment rentals gross profit. Consolidated operating income was $3,973M.

businessLines.name: Specialty
businessLines.how: Same rental model on niche fleets with higher rental gross margins (44% in Q2 2026) and more ancillary and service revenue; grew faster.
businessLines.description: Trench safety, power and HVAC, fluid solutions, mobile storage and other specialty rental businesses (incl. matting/access from the March 2024 Yak acquisition).

operatingProfit.note: United Rentals reports segment equipment rentals gross profit (not segment operating income); this is the profit measure shown, before selling, general and administrative and other costs. Share is of the $5,248M total equipment rentals gross profit. Consolidated operating income was $3,973M.

geography.method: Regional revenue tagged in the filing's own XBRL instance: full-year contexts with one geographic dimension (or segments named after places), alone or crossed only with operating segments or a revenue line of the income statement; regions must add up to the revenue line within 1 percent; a member equal to the sum of others is a subtotal; the main split is the largest set of members adding up to the total; anything not broken out is a computed remainder.
